options: The forms of a single word: its root, pattern and derived forms
The endings of words inside a sentence
The pronunciation of letters in recitation
items.explanation: Ṣarf looks at the word on its own: its pattern and the forms made from its root. Endings in the sentence belong to naḥw.

items.prompt: Which of these words does ṣarf treat as forms of one root?
options: All four: one root, n-ṣ-r, in different patterns
Only naṣara; the others are different words
None: ṣarf does not study verbs
items.explanation: All four share the root letters n-ṣ-r. Ṣarf explains the pattern of each.

items.prompt: Why is ṣarf usually read before naḥw in the madrasa?
options: Naḥw speaks of the endings of words whose forms the student must already recognise
Naḥw is only for advanced students of fiqh
There is no reason; the order is random
items.explanation: A student who cannot recognise a word's form cannot judge its ending, so the books of ṣarf come first.
